correctness.rationale: Assertion 1, RESULT.md line 12, is false as written: irreducible does not imply degree three. Over F_2 take (a,b,c,d)=(1,1,0,1). Then ad−bc=1 and f(T)=T²+T+1 is irreducible, but e_2²=e_2 gives a nonzero idempotent. Thus the issue persists even among perfect tables. The proof at lines 44–48 wrongly infers c≠0 from unqualified irreducibility. The exact correction would be ‘f has degree three and is irreducible’: c=0 gives a fixed line at infinity for a perfect table, and for c≠0 the finite fixed lines are the roots of f. When the cubic is irreducible, f(d/c)=(ad−bc)/c is nonzero, implying perfectness. With the degree condition the counts and group calculation do check: Frobenius orbits give (q−1)(q³−q)/3 tables; independence of the two squares forces all natural-basis changes to be monomial; a fixed antidiagonal change would give a root s, and the only nonidentity diagonal changes have s³=1, t=s² and a=d=0. The exceptional noncube ratios give 2(q−1)²/3 tables, exactly one orbit, and Burnside yields the stated class formulas. The frozen verify.py was read, not run. Its determinant and c≠0 guards (lines 51–60 and 79–87) mean the finite tests do not test bare irreducibility as stated.

evidence: In this perfect two-dimensional family all natural-basis changes are monomial, so the group has order 2s. The joint table counts precisely m=2s/3 labeled order-three matrices in K=0 if g=3 and none otherwise. The remaining T/3−m have trivial stabilizer.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Divide m by its orbit size 2s/3 to obtain one exceptional C_3 class when g=3. Dividing the remaining count by 2s then gives total (T/3−m)/(2s)+m/(2s/3)=q(q+1)/6+(2/3)·1_{g=3}. Thus the full census is a direct corollary, even though the joint record tabulates matrices rather than classes.
